item.title: And another thing
item.content:encoded:
It's a -1 from me, but I want to add something to everything else that people have brought up.

I think this article's issues go farther than being tonal. To be frank, even ignoring the tone, it's just absurdly clunky to read. It's the use of punctuation more than anything. For example:

597 is to be hosed down weekly, with special care given to the areas around the nipples, to prevent the buildup of saliva and drool.

The second comma feels… just randomly there. It's an unnecessary slice in the middle of the sentence. There's no reason to put that beat there. It would feel like a harmless typo if nearly every sentence didn't have the same or similar issues. And listen, I'm not just here to be a stickler about proper punctuation. Honestly, breaking grammar to get a certain emotion across is a part of writing. A Franz Kafka story often has a lot of commas for a lot of long sentences. But in his stories, it meshes with the word choice. It's hard to describe, but I find the language used in a Kafka story (admittedly barring the fact that most of us have only read translations) works with the punctuation. Here, even though some sentences use clinical language, that language is at war with how they're cut up and organized. The word choice is (sometimes) clinical; the sentence structure is not.

The tone has been defended at times by explaining how this article is supposed to feature Foundation personnel becoming enraptured with this SCP. However, since this structure problem is present throughout the article as opposed to gradually shifting into disorganized madness, to me it feels like the article is unpolished. And when that's combined with some of these monolithic paragraphs, it makes me just want to stop reading. My eyes start to roll into the back of my head.

I'm sorry if this is coming across as harsh, and in all fairness I'm likely not a saint when it comes to this as well. But in honesty, it feels weird that in this discussion, the closest others have come to describing this issue is bringing up the tone problem, which for me doesn't quite hit the nail on the head (which perhaps also suggests that I'm the only one bothered by this, so… oh well). Not angry or disappointed in anyone, but seeing that just really made me want to talk about it. As such, I also think that if this is gonna stay up, it definitely needs a rewrite. I know it's Series 1, but personally, I think even by that standard it falls flat.

Regarding the slur, for a really long time, it wasn't considered one— like, it was considered the proper medical term for mental disabilities. It appeared in up to the DSM-4, only to be changed with the publication of the DSM-5 in 2013. This article was written in 2009, so while it hasn't aged well, we can't fault the original author for using what was, at the time, accepted terminology. It would be like criticising Girl with the Dragon Tattoo for using the term "Asperger's Syndrome" instead of "Autistic Spectrum Disorder" when the latter term didn't exist when the book was being written.

That being said… the rest of this article is a bunch of squicky shock value and not much else.

item.content:encoded:
Back when I first read this, I thought it was really great. Now… I see a lot of flaws. The writing is generally good and the ideas are solid, but the tone doesn't match the rest of the site at all, especially the description of its effect in the paragraph beginning "The urge to suckle is a mental, physical, and sexual compulsion." That's far too flowery and sensual for an SCP report.

Here's another paragraph that bugs me:

Men with already unstable or fragile egos find a strengthening in Oedipal Complexes, often to dangerous levels; three employees have raped and murdered [DATA EXPUNGED] These same personality types also enjoy [DATA EXPUNGED] and request access to SCP-597 for that purpose. Unfortunately, although this behavior is not encouraged, those with this disease are many, too many to take a moral or ideological stance and completely restrict the activity without losing the needed number of workers. A good number are also high-level personnel, although revelation of their identity is forbidden, and requires clearing the area and disabling the camera feeds so they can perform the act (which is not allowed to go over an hour, or separation will cause seizures and homicidal tantrums). Specific procedures for sexual visits can be found in See Document 597-XD-12

I can't see the Foundation permitting sexual visits, or allowing people who become this obsessed to remain on duty in any capacity. I also don't see why they would let people become permanently attached to it, as specified in Document 597-XX-23. Would the Foundation really stand for that, or would they take them away and experiment on them to see what would break this thing's hold?

Also not fond of "development of bisexual tendencies" being used as a sign of this thing's negative effects, as it tends to depict same-gender female attraction as some kind of perversion.

I do think it can be fixed, mainly by making the language in the main report more clinical and moving the creepiest stuff into an incident report (as in, a Foundation site didn't contain it properly and went off the deep end), but right now I just don't think it's working.

Downvoted, for many of the reasons expressed by others. Tone issues ("hundreds and hundreds" is just one example), and the following plain old inconsistencies:

They are reduced quickly to an infantile state, and within one hour lose all linguistic abilities, intellectual capabilities, and willpower.

Yet we have a bunch of higher level staff presumably coming to suckle on the nipples and do all kinds of (most likely sexual) [DATA EXPUNGED] to the thing on a regular basis? Considering the fact you apparently need to be in close proximity to 597 (or see it) in order to be affected by it… Why has so much staff (especially supposedly higher level staff) been affected by it? Images carry the effect? Well, by golly, pictures aren't allowed. Security footage is only to be captured via CCTV, and used purely for record keeping if anything happens/monitor cleaning crews or something to make sure they don't get affected.

Also, I don't want some of them removed, but a few of the [DATA EXPUNGED]s don't feel right. They're either covering up something after it's all basically given away, or covering up just a little too much, so the mind doesn't quite have enough to fill in gaps to make it truly creepy.

Going off the comments I've seen here, a fair amount has changed from the original article, and it seems like some things carried over from earlier versions that don't match up well (or at all) with the current version.

Also the thing with vermin needing to be removed… Other than the ones already attached to 597, how would any others get in there with current procedures? Okay, maybe something could get in every now and then, so have new organisms appearing be reported, but the way it's worded now makes it sound like this is a daily occurrence. The way that paragraph is worded is odd as well. It is "to be sealed", measures "are to be put in place"… 1) I expect bug and rodent extermination are generally sort of standard faire for any facility. 2) This is apparently a daily task, considering the "in the morning" line. That's pretty horrible containment there if it's a daily problem and the vermin aren't "magically" being created by the skip or something.

I actually really like the idea of someone possibly being immune to its effects. Like testing determined (as suggested before) that people lactating are unaffected, so they have an all female staff (naturally lactating or via drugs), and they have to be observed by one of the site physicians (who do this for each other) using a breast pump successfully before each shift before being allowed to work. Or does a hazmat suit with a SCBA protect you? The workers apparently wear hazmat suits to clean the containment area already… Easy enough to test, even if we don't want hazmat suits to work.

And I really don't like the whole "if you look at it, even in a picture or video/CCTV/whatever, you are basically screwed" thing. Maybe it's not in a lot of articles, but it takes away from the creep factor in a way when the thing is really only "dangerous" because you're mentally boned if you ever see it, in any way. That works for 096, but I find it lame and annoying in most every other article it's used in.

Sorry this got so long (I probably have even more in me, but need to just stop typing now), and I know it's got a good rating, but it has a lot of glaring issues (tone and the inconsistencies being the main ones I have a problem with and really want to see fixed), and don't feel it's up to current site standards.
